newsitem.title: USA: Troubled Florida Aquarium cuts staff, salaries.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Florida Aquarium cuts staff, salaries.

text.p: Florida Aquarium laid off 44 employees and cut salaries for remaining staff by 10 percent in an effort to cut costs at the struggling Tampa attraction, an aquarium spokeswoman said Tuesday.

The cuts were expected to save $1.4 million in the next year, spokeswoman Wendy Enriquez said. Additionally, several unfilled jobs were eliminated, and advertising and community education programs were cut.
The aquarium had previously cut its annual budget by $1.5 million, but more drastic steps were needed because admission revenues continued to lag operating costs.
The facility has cut its staff to 97 employees, a reduction of more than 40 percent since opening in March 1995, but has had to dip into reserves to meet debt service payments.
City of Tampa took over ownership of the aquarium in October and issued $104 million of revenue bonds to refinance its construction debt.
The refinancing agreement called for the city to pay $4.3 million annually in debt service on the bonds, but city officials have balked at also covering part of the operating losses.
Before the latest round of cuts, city officials said operating losses could reach $2 million by the end of the city's fiscal year on Sept 30.
